title: Bigfoot, Willie Mays and unicorns are coming to stamps
excerpt: New USPS stamps for 2027 will honor Willie Mays and Pat Summitt while featuring mythical creatures, Halloween monsters and more.
content:
Nov. 15, 2026, 4:06 a.m. CT

The U.S. Postal Service plans to honor Pat Summitt and Willie Mays while also putting unicorns, Halloween monsters and some of America's best-known mythical creatures on new stamps in 2027.

The designs are among a partial list of 2027 stamps announced by USPS, according to a community announcement.

More subjects will be announced in the coming weeks and months, and the preliminary designs could change.

Customers can buy stamps and other philatelic products at usps.com/shopstamps, by calling 844-737-7826, by mail through "USA Philatelic" or at Post Office locations nationwide.

Pat Summitt and Willie Mays

Pat Summitt, who coached the University of Tennessee women's basketball program for 38 years, will be featured on a stamp with an oil-on-primed-linen portrait by Roberto Parada.

Summitt, who lived from 1952 to 2016, led Tennessee to 1,098 victories and eight national championships. Ethel Kessler, a USPS art director, designed the stamp.

Baseball legend Willie Mays will be honored on the 50th stamp in the USPS Black Heritage series.

Mays, who lived from 1931 to 2024, won 12 MLB Gold Glove Awards. His stamp is designed as an homage to classic baseball cards, combining a portrait of Mays as a New York Giant with an image of his over-the-shoulder catch during Game 1 of the 1954 World Series.

Known as "The Catch," the play helped lead the New York Giants to a win. The stamp's orange background references a color associated with Mays' career with the New York and San Francisco Giants and New York Mets.

USPS art director Antonio Alcalá designed the stamp using Getty Images photographs.

Unicorns, cryptids and Halloween monsters

A pane of 16 Unicorns stamps will feature four scenes by Kendra Binney. The mixed-media art combines watercolor, acrylic, pencil and digital effects. USPS art director Derry Noyes designed the stamps.

Another set, Mythical Creatures, will put five figures from American folklore on stamps: Mothman, Jackalope, Squonk, Sasquatch and Champ.

Mothman is associated with West Virginia, where reports of the red-eyed, human-size flying creature date to 1966. The Jackalope grew out of a Wyoming creation by taxidermist brothers in the 1930s. Squonk comes from Pennsylvania lumbermen's lore, while Sasquatch, also known as Bigfoot, is closely associated with the Pacific Northwest. Champ is a lake monster from legends surrounding the Lake Champlain region of New York and Vermont.

Artist Nat Power digitally drew the creatures and imagery representing their environments. Alcalá designed the stamps.

USPS also plans four Halloween stamps showing friendly depictions of a vampire, witch, mummy and Frankenstein's monster. Erick Martinez created the artwork, and Alcalá designed the stamps.

Flowers, vegetables and celebrations

The Postal Service will continue its annual floral-stamp tradition with Colorful Blooms, a set of four close-up illustrations of abstract flowers. Magrikie Berg created the illustrations using watercolor and gouache, and Alcalá designed the stamps.

Veggies Forever will be sold as a booklet of 20 stamps with 10 photographs by food photographer Renée Comet. The subjects are a red onion, Savoy cabbage, red cabbage, purple cauliflower, beech mushrooms, purple asparagus, an artichoke, a fairy tale eggplant, rhubarb and a watermelon radish. Kessler designed the stamps.

The new Celebrate stamp is intended for occasions including birthdays, anniversaries, engagements, weddings, new jobs and retirements. Alcalá designed it with artist Jason Gottlieb.

The 2027 Love stamp will feature Lisa Congdon's folk-art-influenced design using geometric shapes, simple colors and imagery intended to evoke joy. Greg Breeding provided art direction.

Lunar New Year, U.S. flag and Lady Liberty

The Postal Service will mark the Year of the Goat with the eighth stamp in its third Lunar New Year series, which began in 2020.

Artist Camille Chew created a cut-paper goat mask for the stamp as part of a series depicting the 12 animals of the Chinese zodiac. Alcalá designed the stamp using Sally Andersen-Bruce's photograph of the mask.

USPS will also mark the 250th anniversary of the Stars and Stripes with a U.S. Flag stamp. Alcalá photographed the flag at Alexandria City Hall in Virginia and designed the stamp.

Another stamp will celebrate "E Pluribus Unum," the nation's founding motto, pairing it with an image of the Statue of Liberty formed from various-size red and blue dots against a white background. Alcalá designed the stamp.

Childhood cancer research and wedding stamps

USPS plans a Cure Childhood Cancers semipostal stamp that will raise money for childhood cancer research. Net proceeds from the stamp's surcharge will be donated to the National Institutes of Health for research intended to improve survival and develop safer, less toxic treatments for children and adolescents with cancer.

According to the announcement, about 15,000 American children and adolescents receive cancer diagnoses annually, and childhood cancer is the leading cause of disease-related death among children after infancy.

Breeding designed the stamp with original artwork by Chuck Styles.

Three additional stamps focus on invitations, weddings and messages of affection.

The 2-ounce You're Invited — Wedding Edition stamp is intended for heavier traditional wedding invitations. Its design uses the words "You're Invited" in calligraphy with flourishes. Artist and calligrapher Nina Tran selected a copperplate lettering style widely used in the 17th and 18th centuries. Alcalá designed the stamp.

The With Love Forever stamp is intended for 1-ounce mail, including wedding RSVP cards, thank-you notes and cards for Valentine's Day, Mother's Day and Father's Day.

The You're Invited — For All Occasions pane will contain 10 Forever stamps in several colors. They are intended for invitations weighing up to 1 ounce, including those for weddings, birthdays, showers, graduations and holiday gatherings.
